entries.title: Deprecated legacy options, methods, and types are removed from the public API
entries.detail: `ScraperOptions` no longer includes the deprecated legacy fields (`includeRawTransaction`, `optInFeatures`, `outputData`, `shouldAddTransactionInformation`, `shouldCombineInstallments`, `usePipeline`, `verbose`), and `createScraper` no longer emits `ScraperOptionsWarning` for them. `IScraper` removes the unimplemented `triggerTwoFactorAuth` and `getLongTermTwoFactorToken` stub methods. `ScraperErrorTypes.General` (`'GENERAL_ERROR'`), `IScraperLoginResult`, `ScraperLoginResult`, the misspelled `ScaperLoginResult` and `ScaperScrapingResult` aliases, `IOutputDataOptions`, `OptInFeatures`, `IFutureDebit`, `IScraperDiagnostics`, `IScraperScrapingResult.futureDebits`, `IScraperScrapingResult.diagnostics`, and `ITransaction.rawTransaction` are also removed.
entries.action: Remove deprecated options from `createScraper({ ... })` calls, switch any `ScraperErrorTypes.General` reference to `ScraperErrorTypes.Generic`, and use `ITransactionsAccount.windowCoverage` and `FORENSIC_TRACE=true` instead of legacy diagnostics or `includeRawTransaction`.
entries.before: createScraper({ companyId, startDate, shouldCombineInstallments: false, includeRawTransaction: true });

entries.title: Behatsdaa and Beyahad Bishvilha are removed; `createScraper` throws for an unknown company
entries.detail: `CompanyTypes.Behatsdaa` (`'behatsdaa'`) and `CompanyTypes.BeyahadBishvilha` (`'beyahadBishvilha'`) are no longer exported, and their `SCRAPERS` entries are gone. They were the last two scrapers on the legacy browser chain, which is removed with them. `createScraper` now resolves every company through the Pipeline registry, so a company id that is not registered throws `ScraperError('unknown company id <id>')` instead of falling back to a legacy scraper. The other 17 institutions are unchanged.
entries.action: Stop passing these two company ids. TypeScript callers see a compile error on the removed enum members; JavaScript callers get the thrown `ScraperError` at `createScraper`. If you still need either institution, pin `^9` until you have another source for it.
entries.after: // Removed: pick a supported company from CompanyTypes, or pin ^9.

entries.title: The browser engine is removed; browser options leave `ScraperOptions`
entries.detail: Every supported bank runs over HTTP, so the Playwright/Camoufox engine, the `postinstall` patch and both browser dependencies are gone. `ScraperOptions` no longer accepts `browser`, `browserContext`, `skipCloseBrowser`, `preparePage`, `defaultTimeout`, `viewportSize`, `shouldShowBrowser`, `executablePath`, `args`, `prepareBrowser`, `timeout`, `storeFailureScreenShotPath` or `navigationRetryCount`. Browser option types and Playwright imports no longer appear in the public declarations. `playwright-core` and `@hieutran094/camoufox-js` are no longer installed, so a consumer install downloads no browser binary and runs no browser patch.
entries.action: Remove those options from `createScraper` calls. A run no longer opens a page, so `page` hooks, viewport and timeout settings have no effect. If your own code imported Playwright types through this package, add `playwright-core` to your dependencies explicitly.
entries.before: createScraper({ companyId, startDate, shouldShowBrowser: false, browser });

entries.title: API-direct login failures name the step and HTTP status
entries.detail: When a login request fails for OneZero, PayBox or Pepper, `errorMessage` is now `<step> HTTP <status>`, for example `login HTTP 401`, or `<step> <errorType>`, for example `bind TIMEOUT`, when no reply arrived. It used to read `<VERB> <url> <status>: ` followed by up to 120 characters of the bank's reply, and a bank can echo the password, the OTP or a device id back in that reply. `errorType` and `errorDetails` are unchanged. A `WAF_BLOCKED` login failure keeps its 9.0.0 message, and failures after login keep the old form.
entries.action: If you read the URL or the bank's reply out of a login failure's `errorMessage`, branch on `errorType` instead; the new message still names the step and the status.

entries.title: Browser options on a browserless bank log a `ScraperOptionsWarning`
entries.detail: A bank that never opens a browser — OneZero and Visa Cal today — ignores browser options. It used to ignore them silently. `createScraper` now emits one `ScraperOptionsWarning` that names every browser option passed for such a bank: `args`, `browser`, `browserContext`, `defaultTimeout`, `executablePath`, `prepareBrowser`, `preparePage`, `shouldShowBrowser`, `timeout` or `viewportSize`. Only option names are printed, never values. The scrape itself is unchanged.
entries.action: Remove the named options from that bank's `createScraper` call to silence the warning. See [Browser options on browserless banks](configuration.md#browser-options-on-browserless-banks).

entries.title: Visa Cal signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Visa Cal now logs in and scrapes over the issuer's API with Node's own `fetch`, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `username` and `password`. A run now also returns `persistentOtpToken`, a hash that changes on every run; passed back as `otpLongTermToken`, it skips the password step. A wrong password fails as `INVALID_PASSWORD` with the message `login outcome 4`.
entries.action: Remove browser options from Visa Cal's `createScraper` call. To skip the password step, store `result.persistentOtpToken` after every run and pass it as `otpLongTermToken` next time; keep `username` and `password` too, because a rejected hash falls back to a full login.

entries.title: Isracard signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Isracard now logs in and scrapes over its mobile gateway with Node's own `fetch` and a cookie jar, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `id`, `card6Digits` and `password`. A cold login registers a device key and returns it as `persistentOtpToken`; the key stays the same from run to run, and passed back as `otpLongTermToken` it skips the password step. The session rides on cookies, so `onAuthFlowComplete` receives an empty `bearer`. A wrong password still fails as `INVALID_PASSWORD`, now with the message `login outcome unmapped`.
entries.action: Remove browser options from Isracard's `createScraper` call. To skip the password step, store `result.persistentOtpToken` and pass it as `otpLongTermToken`; keep `id`, `card6Digits` and `password` too, because a rejected key falls back to a full login. Do not read `bearer` from `onAuthFlowComplete` for Isracard.

entries.title: Max signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Max now logs in and scrapes over its website's API with Node's own `fetch`, keeping the run's cookies, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `username` and `password`. There is no long-term token: every run logs in with the password, and `persistentOtpToken` stays unset. entries.title: Mizrahi signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Mizrahi now logs in and scrapes over its website's JSON API with Node's own `fetch` and one cookie jar, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. entries.title: Hapoalim signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Hapoalim now logs in and scrapes over its website's API with Node's own `fetch` and one cookie jar, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `userCode` and `password`. The SMS step runs only when the bank asks for it: `otpCodeRetriever`, from the credentials or the options, receives the masked phone number, and if the bank asks while no retriever was passed the run fails as `TWO_FACTOR_RETRIEVER_MISSING`. A run now also returns `persistentOtpToken`, a `v1.` token holding the session cookies; passed back as `otpLongTermToken`, it skips the login and the SMS. A locked or disabled account fails as `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`, a password the bank wants replaced as `CHANGE_PASSWORD`, any other state the password check returns as `GENERIC` with the message `verify outcome unmapped`, and a reply that carries a bank error as `GENERIC` with `verify bank error`. A wrong password may therefore fail as `GENERIC` rather than `INVALID_PASSWORD`. Failed data calls now name the call and HTTP status instead of the request URL (for example, `transactions HTTP 500`). No failure message carries the bank's own text.
entries.action: Remove browser options from Hapoalim's `createScraper` call and keep passing `otpCodeRetriever`. To skip the login and the SMS, store `result.persistentOtpToken` after every run and pass it as `otpLongTermToken` next time. The token is a live session, so store it as a secret. Keep `userCode`, `password` and the retriever too, because a refused session falls back to a full login with one SMS.

entries.title: Yahav signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Yahav now logs in and scrapes over its mobile app's API through `node:https` and one cookie jar, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `num` (or the legacy `username`), `nationalID` and `password`. They are checked before any request: a blank `num`, a `nationalID` that is not all digits or a `password` outside Latin-1 fails as `GENERIC` with `Missing or malformed credentials`. A cold login enrols the run as a device of the customer, which may sign the customer's phone app out. Wrong credentials draw a `401` at that enrolment and fail as `INVALID_PASSWORD`, with the message `register HTTP 401`; the reply names no reason, so every `401` there is reported the same way. A run returns `persistentOtpToken`, a `v1.` token holding that device, its private key and the session cookies; passed back as `otpLongTermToken`, it skips the enrolment. Login and failed data calls omit the bank's response text from failure messages.
entries.action: Remove browser options from Yahav's `createScraper` call. Store `result.persistentOtpToken` after every run and pass it as `otpLongTermToken` next time, so a run enrols a device only when it must. The token holds a private key, so store it as a secret. Keep `num`, `nationalID` and `password` too, because a token the bank rejects with a `401` or `403` falls back to a full login. If the bank keeps refusing the token with a `400`, drop it once so the next run enrols afresh.

entries.title: Beinleumi signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Beinleumi now logs in and scrapes over its web login API on `online.fibi.co.il` with Node's own `fetch` and one cookie jar, so no browser starts. Browser options passed for it no longer apply: `createScraper` names them in a `ScraperOptionsWarning` and ignores them, so a `preparePage` hook or a caller's `browser` is not used. Credentials are still `username` and `password`; a blank one fails as `GENERIC` with `Missing or malformed credentials` before any request. The SMS step runs only when the bank asks for it: `otpCodeRetriever`, from the credentials or the options, is called with an empty hint, and if the bank asks while no retriever was passed the run fails as `TWO_FACTOR_RETRIEVER_MISSING`. A code of the wrong length fails before it is sent. A password the bank refuses fails as `INVALID_PASSWORD` and a refused code as `INVALID_OTP`. Device memory is opt-in: with `onPersistentAuthStateUpdate`, a run that starts with no stored state hands the callback a state naming the provider, the lower-cased `username` and the device id the bank issued, with no password or token; passed back as `persistentAuthState`, that id is sent on later logins and the bank may skip the SMS. No failure message carries the bank's own text.
entries.action: Remove browser options from Beinleumi's `createScraper` call and keep passing `otpCodeRetriever`, because the bank decides when it asks for a code. To let the bank remember the device, pass `onPersistentAuthStateUpdate`, store the state it receives and pass it back as `persistentAuthState` on later runs.

entries.title: Discount signs in without a browser
entries.detail: Discount now logs in and scrapes over its web API on `start.telebank.co.il`, with Node's own `fetch` and one cookie jar, so no browser starts. entries.title: Node 24.11 or later required; Node 22 is no longer supported
entries.detail: `engines.node` is now `>= 24.11.0`, the first Node 24 LTS release, and the published bundle is compiled for Node 24. CI no longer tests Node 22, which reaches end-of-life on 2027-04-30. On an older runtime npm warns at install, or fails under `engine-strict`. The public API is unchanged.
entries.action: Upgrade to Node 24.11 or later before installing 9.x; `node --version` must print v24.11.0 or higher. If you must stay on Node 22, pin `^8` until you can upgrade; 8.x does not get the other 9.0.0 changes, including the OneZero fix.

entries.title: OneZero needs OpenSSL 3.5
entries.detail: OneZero's Cloudflare edge now admits only clients whose TLS handshake matches the OneZero Android app. The scraper sends that handshake, but only OpenSSL 3.5 or later can produce it. Every official Node build from 24.11.0, the new minimum, bundles it. A Node built against an older shared or system OpenSSL does not: building the OneZero transport then logs a `warn` line, `[tls] runtime OpenSSL cannot emit this TLS profile; the bank edge may block requests`, and the login fails with `WAF_BLOCKED`. No other institution is affected.
entries.action: None on an official Node build. If your Node links a shared or system OpenSSL and you scrape OneZero, `node -p process.versions.openssl` must print 3.5 or higher.

entries.title: API-direct Cloudflare block pages and challenges report `WAF_BLOCKED`
entries.detail: When Cloudflare refuses an API-direct request with a `4xx` block page, OneZero now reports `WAF_BLOCKED` instead of `GENERIC`. The message keeps its `<VERB> <url> <status>: ` prefix but ends `blocked by Cloudflare edge (WAF) before reaching the API` instead of quoting the page, which embeds your IP and a Ray ID. A Cloudflare challenge, recognised by its `cf-mitigated: challenge` response header at any status, is reported the same way with a message ending `challenged by Cloudflare edge (WAF) before reaching the API`. `WAF_BLOCKED` is terminal: the call is not re-minted, and a blocked warm start no longer falls back to an SMS login. PayBox and Pepper already reported `WAF_BLOCKED` when a page contained any Cloudflare marker. They now need a `4xx` HTML page carrying Cloudflare's block markers, or the challenge header, so a Cloudflare `5xx` origin error, or an unrelated page that happens to contain `oldie`, reports `GENERIC`. `errorDetails` is not set on this path.
entries.action: If you branch on `errorType`, handle `WAF_BLOCKED` for API-direct banks as well. Code that matched Cloudflare page text inside `errorMessage` should match the new reason instead.

entries.title: A `warn` line when the browser stack differs from the tested pair
entries.detail: Each release is tested against one Camoufox build and one `playwright-core` minor. After the first successful Camoufox launch in a process, the installed versions are compared with that pair, and each component that differs is logged once at `warn` level as `browser stack differs from the tested pair`, with `component`, `installed`, `tested` and `remedy`. A different version often works, so the check never fails a launch.
entries.action: None. If a scrape breaks while this line is logged, follow its `remedy`. See Troubleshooting for each field and how to return to the tested pair.

entries.title: Known limitation: `httpCredentials` fails on `playwright-core` 1.63 and 1.64
entries.detail: From 1.63, `playwright-core` sends a context's `httpCredentials` as a list, and no Camoufox release checked so far accepts one. `browser.newContext({ httpCredentials })` then fails with `Protocol error (Browser.setHTTPCredentials)`. This library never sets `httpCredentials`, so its own scrapes are unaffected. CI has tested 1.63 since 8.7.2, and the `^1.62.0` range let a fresh install resolve 1.63 before that.
entries.action: Don't create a context with `httpCredentials` for this library, for example one you pass in as `browserContext`. No `playwright-core` minor this library tests supports it with Camoufox yet.

entries.title: `playwright-core` 1.64 supported
entries.detail: `playwright-core` 1.64 changed two things no released Camoufox follows yet, and the `postinstall` patch now adapts both. It sends a new `bypassServiceWorker` field when it turns on request interception, which Camoufox rejects, so `page.route()` failed with a protocol error. `context.route()` was unaffected: Firefox turns on context-wide interception through a different call. The patch drops that field and sends the 1.63 payload. 1.64 also stopped splitting the `Set-Cookie` lines Camoufox reports as one header, so `headersArray()` and `headerValues('set-cookie')` returned one merged entry instead of one per cookie, and nothing reported an error. The patch splits them again. CI now tests this library on 1.64.
entries.action: None when install scripts run. With `--ignore-scripts`, run `node node_modules/@sergienko4/israeli-bank-scrapers/scripts/patch-playwright-core.mjs` after installing. See Troubleshooting for the routing error text.

entries.title: Camoufox browser engine upgraded to 0.11.x
entries.detail: `@hieutran094/camoufox-js` moved from ^0.6.8 to ^0.11.2. Camoufox supplies the hardened Firefox build used to get past bank WAFs, so this changes which browser binary is downloaded on first run.
entries.action: Clear any cached Camoufox download so the new engine is fetched. If scraping starts failing right after this upgrade, remove the cache directory and re-run once.

entries.title: `OneZeroScraper` is no longer exported
entries.detail: OneZero moved onto the declarative Pipeline, and the standalone `OneZeroScraper` class was removed from the public surface. This shipped in a minor release without a breaking-change note - it is recorded here so the gap is visible.
entries.action: Construct OneZero through the factory instead of importing the class directly. Every other bank already used this form, so most callers are unaffected.
entries.before:
import { OneZeroScraper } from '@sergienko4/israeli-bank-scrapers';

const scraper = new OneZeroScraper(options);
entries.after:
import createScraper, { CompanyTypes } from '@sergienko4/israeli-bank-scrapers';

const scraper = createScraper({ ...options, companyId: CompanyTypes.oneZero });

entries.title: Switched from `playwright` to `playwright-core`
entries.detail: `playwright` bundles a browser download step; `playwright-core` does not. Browsers for this library come from Camoufox, so the download was redundant and made installs much heavier.
entries.action: None for normal use. If your own code imported `playwright` transitively through this package, add it to your dependencies explicitly.
